intent: Produce distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping existing UI, with deliberate aesthetic direction, typography and layout choices specific to the brief.
steps: Ground the design in the subject: name the concrete subject, audience and the page primary job when the brief does not pin them down
Derive distinctive choices from the subject world rather than generic template defaults
Define a compact token system with named palette, typography roles, layout concept and a single signature element
Review the plan against the brief and revise parts that read like generic defaults for any similar page
Build to the revised plan, deriving every color and type decision from it
Apply motion deliberately where it serves the subject; prefer orchestrated moments over scattered effects
Match implementation complexity to the chosen vision
Write copy from the end user perspective with active voice and consistent vocabulary through the flow
Apply restraint: one memorable signature element with disciplined surroundings
Meet a quality floor: responsive layout, visible keyboard focus, and reduced motion respected
Critique the result during build and remove decoration that does not serve the brief
invariants: The brief own words win when they pin a visual direction
Avoid templated default aesthetics when the brief leaves an axis free
Copy and structure must serve comprehension, not decoration alone
